Microeconomics.Behavioral and Experimental Economics: Controlled laboratory experiments and field experiments testing decision-making, fairness, risk preferences, cooperation, and social norms.
Microeconomics.Industrial Organization Empirics: Empirical studies of market structure, competition, pricing strategies, and firm behavior using observational, experimental, and quasi-experimental methods.
Microeconomics.Labor Economics Empirical: Field and survey-based studies on labor supply, wage determination, hiring discrimination, and the effects of policies on employment outcomes.
Microeconomics.Consumer Behavior and Demand Analysis: Experimental and observational research on consumer choice, preference elicitation, and behavioral biases in purchasing decisions.

Macroeconomics and Public Economics.Empirical Macroeconomics: Econometric and experimental studies on business cycles, monetary/fiscal policy effects, inflation, unemployment, and macro-level interventions.
Macroeconomics and Public Economics.Development Economics: Field experiments, randomized controlled trials, and quasi-experimental designs studying poverty alleviation, microfinance, education, and health in developing countries.
Macroeconomics and Public Economics.Public Economics: Empirical evaluation of taxation, social welfare programs, public goods provision, and policy experiments.

Financial Economics.Behavioral Finance: Laboratory and field experiments studying biases in investment decisions, market anomalies, and financial decision-making under risk and uncertainty.
Financial Economics.Empirical Market Analysis: Data-driven analysis of asset pricing, market microstructure, trading behavior, and portfolio strategies using historical or high-frequency data.

Health and Education Economics.Health Economics: Randomized controlled trials and quasi-experimental studies of healthcare interventions, insurance design, and health behavior responses.
Health and Education Economics.Education Economics: Empirical studies and experiments on school interventions, teaching methods, policy impacts, and educational outcomes.

Environmental and Resource Economics.Field and Lab Experiments on Environment: Experimental and observational research on resource use, climate policy interventions, carbon pricing, and sustainable behavior incentives.

Experimental Methods and Econometrics.Experimental Design and Methodology: Development and application of lab, field, and online experimental designs for causal inference in economics.
Experimental Methods and Econometrics.Applied Econometrics: Empirical research applying statistical and econometric methods to real-world data, including natural experiments, panel data, and instrumental variables approaches.

Neuroeconomics and Cognitive Economics.Neuroeconomic Experiments: Experimental studies combining behavioral economics and neuroscience (e.g., fMRI, EEG) to understand decision-making, valuation, and risk perception.
Neuroeconomics and Cognitive Economics.Cognitive and Psychophysiological Experi: Research on attention, memory, and cognitive processes affecting economic behavior using lab-based experimental paradigms.

Field and Natural Experiments.Policy and Program Evaluation: Empirical analysis using natural experiments, randomized field trials, and quasi-experimental methods to measure policy impacts.
Field and Natural Experiments.Market and Organizational Field Experime: Controlled interventions in real-world market or organizational settings to test economic theories and behavior.
